name: Moonstone Harbinger
description:
Flying, deathtouch

Once each turn, whenever you gain life during your turn, Bats you control get +1/+0 and gain deathtouch until end of turn.

Once each turn, whenever you lose life during your turn, Bats you control get +1/+0 and gain deathtouch until end of turn.
assumptions: Grouped the two bare keyword grants (nodes C and D — static `modifier` edges onto `self` with flags `flying` and `deathtouch` respectively) onto one printed line, "Flying, deathtouch," per standard Magic templating for multiple keyword abilities with no other attached text — even though they're two separate `flow` roots rather than one combine group.

Interpreted `thing: "bat"` on nodes F and H as "Bats you control." It isn't one of the schema's three reserved `thing` values, isn't a coarse type-line word, and doesn't match any registry key (the registry only has `bat-1`, a token template, which would mean creating a Bat token — but F/H are `modifier` nodes, not `enters`, so no token is being made). "Bats you control" is the closest reading, treating "bat" as an implicit subtype filter over permanents the caster (owner: me) controls, with no `target`/`not:self` flag restricting it further.

Worded the paired flags `cond:once_per_turn` + `cond:your_turn` on triggers E and G as "Once each turn, whenever you gain/lose life during your turn," — the flags fix both logical conditions (fires only once per turn; fires only during my own turn) but not their literal phrasing, since the nodes don't carry printed text.

Treated nodes A (cast) and B (enters) as producing no separate printed ability — they represent the ordinary cast-resolve-enter-battlefield sequence for a creature spell, not a triggered/static ability in their own right.
couldNotDerive: Whether the two triggered abilities (lifegained-based and lifelost-based) are meant to read as a single combined ability text-wise or as fully independent lines — the flow graph gives them as two separate roots (E and G) with no shared grouping construct, so they're presented as two paragraphs, but no reminder/connective text between them is given by the nodes.
Supertype and rarity — omitted per instructions, since neither the self registry nor the nodes determine them.
notes: Mana cost, type line, P/T, both static keywords (flying/deathtouch), and the pump/deathtouch-grant effect wording all matched the real card exactly — no gap there. The real issue is a functional one, not presentational: the real Oracle text is ONE ability with a compound trigger condition and a single shared cap — 'Whenever you gain or lose life during your turn, Bats you control get +1/+0 and gain deathtouch until end of turn. This ability triggers only once each turn.' The Forge script backs this with two T: lines sharing one Execute$ (TrigPump): `T:Mode$ LifeGained | ... | ActivationLimit$ 1 | PlayerTurn$ True | ...` and `T:Mode$ LifeLost | ... | ActivationLimit$ 1 | PlayerTurn$ True | Secondary$ True | ...` — the `Secondary$ True` field is Forge's own marker that the second trigger is the same named ability as the first (identical TriggerDescription on both lines), not an independent one. `grep -n "Secondary" app/lib/forgeTranslate.ts` returns zero matches — the translator has no handling of `Secondary$` at all. Its trigger builder (around the `onceFlag = fields.ActivationLimit === '1' ... 'cond:once_per_turn'` line and the per-trigger node/downstream-chain construction that follows) processes each T: line as a fully independent pass, so it emits two separate root trigger nodes (E: trigger-type lifegained, G: trigger-type lifelost), each independently carrying its own `cond:once_per_turn`, each feeding its own separately-built modifier node (F under E, H under G) with identical flags. Net effect: the edges graph encodes up to 2 activations per turn (one via a gain event satisfying E's own once-per-turn budget, one via a loss event satisfying G's separate budget), where the real card allows only 1 activation per turn total regardless of which event type causes it — a real rules divergence, not just a wording/paragraph split. Contrast with two precedents already in this exam set that share the identical Secondary$-pair shape but were correctly judged 'match': Carrot Cake (ChangesZone/Sacrificed pair, Secondary$ True, no ActivationLimit on either — naturally single-fire per event, no double-count possible) and Wax-Wane Witness (identical LifeGained/LifeLost pair, no ActivationLimit at all — unlimited activation from either event IS the real behavior). Moonstone Harbinger is the first case where BOTH members of a Secondary$ pair carry their own ActivationLimit$1, and the existing per-trigger cond:once_per_turn handling (correct in isolation, per Caretaker's Talent's exam) doesn't compose across a Secondary$-linked pair — it should recognize the two ActivationLimit$1s as one shared per-turn budget rather than two independent ones. This is both a decomposition/translator gap (forgeTranslate.ts needs Secondary$ handling that links the pair's activation counters) and a SCHEMA.md gap (no existing flag vocabulary expresses two root trigger nodes sharing one once-per-turn counter — the `:=`/`=` binding convention only covers scaler/variable values, not a cap shared across nodes). Secondary, non-blocking: `thing: "bat"` on nodes F/H is an ungoverned bare subtype string — not a registry key, not one of the three reserved `thing` words, not a coarse type-line word — so its correct reading as "Bats you control" depended entirely on the reconstructing agent's own inference rather than anything the schema/registries actually fix; it happened to land correctly here but is a latent registries.json completeness gap worth closing. Packet itself was read correctly by the reconstructing agent (confirmed against its full-message report); this is a genuine decomposition/translator issue, not a process error.
